![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14212914/assets/4b441f7b59f59240141380711d5d380ea58cafa01f8a288f1e5c8bc7685650cf.png)

Consider the diagram shown above, where $\overset{\to }{PS}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{SQ}=b,$ and $\overset{\to }{PT}=c.$ Find $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ in terms of $a,b$ and $c.$
question.worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $P$ to $Q$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,$ and $c.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{PQ}=\overset{\to }{PS}+\overset{\to }{SQ}
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14212914/assets/1bf9ce3f20027a3ce358f8a0a9d72107f087021ca698e677df367e05a7c3e5bb.png)

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{PS}=a,\,\overset{\to }{SQ}=b.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14212914/assets/6b37dcafa2b2b913d7e5328e19257c4d873c5877186df24626033fec8216da05.png)

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =\overset{\to }{PS}+\overset{\to }{SQ} \\  & =a+b\end{aligned}
$$
